record.title: Discrete geometry and automorphic forms (problem 22)
record.statement:
Suppose we have a radial function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($0 < n < 10$) such that $f$ has a single root at $\sqrt{2}$, double roots at $\sqrt{2k}$ for $k > 1$, and $\hat f$ has double roots at $\sqrt{2k}$ for $k \geq 1$. Then, 

$$
\frac{f(0)}{\hat f(0)} = - \frac{(n^4 -56n^3 + 1184n^2 - 11200 n+ 40320}{16(n-10)(n-14)(n-18)}
$$
record.source_name: AimPL: Discrete geometry and automorphic forms (posed by Cohn)

record.title: Discrete geometry and automorphic forms (problem 25)

record.title: The Problems (problem 22)
record.statement: Let $\Pi K$ be the projection body of $K$. It is known that if $K$ is a polytope and $\Pi \Pi K$ is homothetic to $K$, then $K$ is a direct sum of planar polygons (in even dimensions) or a direct sum of planar polygons and a segment (in odd dimensions). If $K$ is an arbitrary convex body and $\Pi \Pi K$ is homothetic to $K$, what can we conclude about $K$?

record.title: Kahler Currents
record.statement:
Show that singular Kahler-Einstein metrics (or more generally singular cscK metrics) are in fact Kahler currents. This was shown in [GGZ] (2022) under suitable assumptions. This is known in dimension $\leq 3$, but it would be nice to understand it more generally.

One could also ask this for singular Kahler almost-Einstein metrics, or given integral Ricci lower bounds.

record.title: Critical height conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$, not Latt\`es. Define the critical height
 

$$
\hat{h}_{crit}(f) = \sum_{c \in \text{crit}(f)} \hat{h}(c).
$$

 Does there exist $c_1,c_2 > 0$ depending on $d,h_M$ such that for all $f \in M_d(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}) - \{\text{Latt\`es}\}$ such that
 

$$
c_1h_M(f) - c_2 \leq \hat{h}_{crit}(f)?
$$

record.title: Lower bounds (problem 2)
record.statement:
Is there a bounded sequence $a(n)$ such that each $a(n)$ is computable in time $O(\log^A n)$ for some fixed $A > 0$ and such that

$$
\left| \sum_{n \leq X} \lambda(n) a(n) \right| > \epsilon X
$$

for all $X$ and some fixed $\epsilon > 0$? Can we say something about the Furstenberg systems of such an $a(n)$? In particular, do they have positive entropy?

record.title: Function-specific mixing time and concentration
record.statement:
Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all $\varepsilon>0$ and $n\geq 1$,

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(\Big| S_n-\mathbb{E} S_n\Big| \geq\varepsilon\right)\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{cn\varepsilon^2}{t_f(\delta)}\right)\,,
$$

where $t_f(\delta)=\sup_{x\in\Omega}\left\{n\geq 0,\, \Big|\mathbb{E}_x f(X_n) -\mathbb{E}_\pi f\Big|\leq\delta\right\}$ ? Does it hold for $\delta=1/4$?

record.title: #32 Improving bound from $1/N^2$ to $1/N$ on grid graphs
record.statement: In a uniformly random spanning tree of a grid graph with $N$ vertices, we know the probability of having an exactly balanced split edge is at least $\frac{1}{N^2}$. Can we improve this to $\frac{1}{N}$? Empirically, this seems like the right answer. It would suffice to extend the $\frac{1}{N^2}$ lower bound to a neighborhood of other edges around the central edge.
record.source_name: AimPL: Mathematical foundations of sampling connected balanced graph partitions

record.title: #10 Uniform partition sampling
record.statement: Can we sample a uniformly random balanced graph partition into two pieces in polynomial time on well-behaved graphs? Specifically, can we do this on grid graphs? Wesley Pegden has an informal argument suggesting that simply running the flip walk would not mix in polynomial-time, so that does not work. Also, what if we drop the balance constraint?
record.source_name: AimPL: Mathematical foundations of sampling connected balanced graph partitions

record.title: #17 Models of graphs arising in real geographic data
record.statement:
-

(a) What is a good generative model?

(b) Perturbed Delaunay triangulations of random point sets seem to work very well. You add edges with preferential attachment then delete edges randomly. Can we formally investigate how/why this works? What about Voronoi graphs or 2-Delaunay graphs?

(c) What about taking a Delaunay triangulation of a non-uniformly random point set?
